title: Kubernetes Troubleshooting: Root Cause Analysis & Outage Remediation
summary: Master production root cause analysis: diagnose CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, OOMKilled, and restore corrupted static pod control planes and misconfigured Kubelets.
learningObjectives: Diagnose and remediate application Pod lifecycle failures including CrashLoopBackOff, missing ConfigMap/Secret keys, and OOMKilled events.
Perform deep-dive control plane diagnostics on static pods (/etc/kubernetes/manifests) and recover unresponsive kube-apiserver instances.
Utilize ephemeral debug containers (kubectl debug) and Kubelet journal logs to isolate node and container failures.

curriculumModules.title: Workload Failure Modes: CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff & OOMKilled
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Kubernetes surfaces distinct container failure states in pod status. CrashLoopBackOff indicates rapid process termination with exponential backoff delays. ImagePullBackOff points to invalid registry credentials or non-existent image tags. OOMKilled (Exit Code 137) occurs when memory exceeds cgroup limits.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Inspect pod termination reasons using kubectl describe pod and kubectl logs --previous to capture stderr traces before pod restart cycles wipe ephemeral logs.

curriculumModules.title: Static Pod & Control Plane Failure Recovery
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Control-plane static pods (kube-apiserver, etcd, kube-controller-manager) are supervised by Kubelet reading manifests in /etc/kubernetes/manifests. A YAML indentation error or certificate expiry stops the apiserver completely, causing kubectl connection refused errors.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Validate static pod manifest syntax with linters before saving edits, and check /var/log/pods or crictl logs on the control plane node when apiserver fails to start.

curriculumModules.title: Node & Kubelet Diagnostics: Ephemeral Containers & Systemd Logs
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: When worker nodes enter NotReady status, root cause analysis requires inspecting Kubelet systemd journals (journalctl -u kubelet -p err) and examining container runtime socket responsiveness (/run/containerd/containerd.sock).
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Use ephemeral debug containers (kubectl debug -it <pod> --image=busybox --target=<container>) to attach interactive diagnostic tools without mutating production distroless images.

labs.title: Diagnosing & Fixing CrashLoopBackOff and OOMKilled Failures
labs.scenario: Microservice payment-processor in namespace troubleshoot-apps is stuck in CrashLoopBackOff due to a missing ConfigMap payment-config and insufficient memory limits (64Mi). Create the required ConfigMap with DB_HOST=postgres.troubleshoot-apps.svc, increase container memory limits to 256Mi, and verify the Deployment achieves healthy Running status.
labs.productionContext: Over 70% of production Kubernetes workload outages stem from configuration drift (missing ConfigMaps/Secrets) or aggressive memory limits triggering kernel OOM killer terminations.
objectives: Create namespace troubleshoot-apps for isolated debugging
Create missing ConfigMap payment-config with DB_HOST literal
Deploy payment-processor with 256Mi memory limits to prevent OOMKilled
Verify all deployment pods reach healthy Running status

steps.title: Create Debugging Namespace
steps.instruction: Create namespace `troubleshoot-apps` using `kubectl create namespace troubleshoot-apps`.

steps.title: Author Patched Deployment Manifest
steps.instruction: Create `/home/learner/payment-processor.yaml` with 256Mi memory limit and apply it.

steps.title: Verify Rollout Status
steps.instruction: Verify deployment rollout reaches complete state.

validationRules.name: payment-processor

validationRules.description: Verified at least 2 ready replicas in payment-processor deployment
validationRules.name: payment-processor

solutionCommands:
echo -e "apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: payment-processor
  namespace: troubleshoot-apps
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: payment-processor
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: payment-processor
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: processor
        image: nginx:1.27-alpine
        resources:
          limits:
            memory: 256Mi
            cpu: 500m
          requests:
            memory: 128Mi
            cpu: 100m" > /home/learner/payment-processor.yaml
labs.troubleshootingGuide: Ensure namespace troubleshoot-apps exists, ConfigMap payment-config is created, and payment-processor Deployment has 2 replicas with 256Mi memory limit.

labs.title: Control Plane Recovery: Static Pod Manifests & Kubelet Diagnostics
labs.scenario: A control-plane node failure occurred where static pod manifest /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml was corrupted. Inspect the manifest using cat, repair the manifest syntax error, restart the Kubelet service using systemctl restart kubelet, and verify cluster component statuses.
labs.productionContext: Control plane outages require cluster administrators to bypass kubectl and directly troubleshoot node filesystems, static pod manifests, and systemd daemons to recover cluster quorum.
objectives: Write valid static pod manifest configuration
Restart Kubelet daemon via systemctl restart kubelet
Verify cluster node health via kubectl get nodes

steps.title: Verify Cluster Health
steps.instruction: Check node status using `kubectl get nodes`.

solutionCommands:
echo -e "apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: kube-apiserver
  namespace: kube-system
spec:
  containers:
  - name: kube-apiserver
    image: registry.k8s.io/kube-apiserver:v1.31.0" > /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml
labs.troubleshootingGuide: Inspect /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml with cat, repair the manifest with valid Pod YAML, restart kubelet, and verify nodes.

assessmentQuestions.question: What is the key diagnostic indicator that distinguishes a container terminated due to OOMKilled from a container failing due to an application exception CrashLoopBackOff?
options: (Recommended) OOMKilled containers exit with exit code 137 (SIGKILL 128 + 9) and show 'OOMKilled: true' in 'kubectl describe pod', whereas application exceptions usually exit with non-zero exit codes (e.g. 1) without OOMKilled flags.
OOMKilled pods always restart on a different node immediately.
Application exceptions cause the worker node to enter NotReady state.
OOMKilled pods are automatically scaled up by the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Exit code 137 indicates that the Linux kernel OOM killer sent SIGKILL (signal 9: 128 + 9 = 137) because the container exceeded its cgroup memory limit. This is explicitly surfaced as 'OOMKilled: true' under Last State in 'kubectl describe pod'.

assessmentQuestions.question: When debugging a distroless container that lacks curl, bash, netstat, or ping, what is the modern Kubernetes-native mechanism to inspect its network namespace and filesystem without rebuilding the container image?
options: (Recommended) Execute 'kubectl debug -it <pod> --image=<debug-image> --target=<container>' to launch an ephemeral container sharing the process and network namespace.
SSH directly into the container using standard openssh keys.
Edit the Deployment spec to add apt-get install curl commands.
Scale the Deployment to zero and back to one replica.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Ephemeral debug containers ('kubectl debug -it ... --target=...') allow administrators to attach a full-featured troubleshooting image (e.g., nicolaka/netshoot or busybox) directly into the running Pod's process and network namespace without modifying or rebuilding the distroless image.
